event: Daily Intelligence Briefing
title: Daily Market Briefing
text:
BOTTOM LINE — Defensive tape, yield-hounded industrials cracked.
NY Fed 1-yr inflation forecast spiked to 3.9% vs 3.64% fc and a 10-yr auction cleared at 5.30% vs 4.83% prior, so long-duration cyclicals and precious metals got sold; only healthcare and utilities held green. Low volume (SPY 0.7x, QQQ 0.8x) means this was drift, not distribution.

INDICES — VIX 15.1, below its 15.8 20-day MA. Ranked: SPY -0.24%, QQQ -0.25%, DIA -0.69%, SOXX -1.12%, IWM -1.29%. Large > small by 1.03pp. Biggest cross-asset move: SLV -2.94%, with GLD -1.67%

VOLUME & BREADTH — SPY vol_ratio 0.7x and QQQ 0.8x: both quiet, and with price down that is apathy rather than distribution. Sector volume favored XLRE 1.5x, XLU 1.4x, XLV 1.1x — defensive rotation on real volume. Breadth diverges badly: only 28% of S&P names above the 50-DMA, 44% above the 200-DMA, adv/dec 146/351, up/down volume 0.59, and 16 new 60-day highs against 78 lows — participation is far weaker than the index suggests.

SECTORS & ROTATION — XLV Healthcare +1.03%, XLU Utilities -0.02%, XLP Staples -0.12%, XLK Technology -0.30%, XLY Discretionary -0.32%, XLC Comms -0.35%, XLF Financials -0.48%, XLE Energy -0.61%, XLRE Real Estate -1.29%, XLB Materials -1.51%, XLI Industrials -2.18%. Top industries: UNG +2.70%, DRAM +0.82%; bottom: URA -4.47%, WGMI -4.25%. Flows confirm defensives: XLU +$2,128mm (100th pctile) and XLK +$611mm in, versus XLF -$795mm (15th pctile) and XLB -$206mm (10th) out. Money is leaving financials, materials and industrials for utilities and healthcare — defensive risk-off.

POSITIONING — SPY PCR 0.70 with skew +3.8% and QQQ PCR 1.52, so QQQ carries real protection demand while SPY is complacent; SPY sits above its 790 GEX flip, so no dealer amplification yet. VIX 15.1 under its 15.8 MA versus VIXEQ 39.1 with a 37.9 MA — the wide VIXEQ-over-VIX gap signals high single-stock dispersion and low implied correlation, a rotation tape, not a macro one.

CROSS-ASSET — Dollar strength (UUP +0.48%) plus the 5.30% 10-year auction yield crushed silver and gold, and the same yield spike is why CAT and the industrial complex sold off. Next FOMC is Oct 28; Polymarket prices 84% no change and 16% for a 25bp hike, hike odds down 2pp over five days.

SIGNALS & WATCH — Fear & Greed 56.1, Neutral. Movers: CAT -5.75% (FTC/USDA comment request), SPOT +5.08%, EME -4.83%, MDT -1.81%. Vol spikes: MDT 3.1x (Medtech 7) and CEG 2.1x (Power 7), both on down days — distribution. Watch XLI (-2.18%) into tomorrow's jobless claims, IWM -1.29% with RVX 21.0 above its 20.5 MA, and XLU on that 100th-percentile inflow.
